paragraphs: This is the neutral dispute resolution occupational group: arbitrators review the evidence and issue an award under the applicable procedure; mediators help the parties reach a voluntary agreement; U.S. conciliators usually meet the parties separately, and whether a recommendation binds the parties must be agreed in advance. Civil and commercial arbitration, people's mediation and labour dispute arbitration in China are governed by different laws, and the subpoena, oath or claim payment authority in the U.S. task list cannot be used directly for Chinese posts. The usual outputs are an issues list, an evidence index, a procedural record, an arbitral award or an agreement between the parties. The scope of Chinese civil and commercial arbitration is disputes over contracts and other property rights and interests between equal parties; disputes over marriage, adoption, guardianship, maintenance and inheritance and administrative disputes that should be handled by administrative organs in accordance with the law cannot be arbitrated under that law. People's mediation handles civil disputes and charges no fee.

Three small self-test tasks: using public materials, write a procedural progress memorandum for a fictional contract price dispute (the matters in dispute, the applicable basis, the hearing or mediation steps to be taken, and the evidence to be supplied); using fictional materials, write an opening statement for a mediation meeting (explaining the procedure, the principles of confidentiality and voluntariness, the timetable and the next steps to the parties); and write up one mediation outcome as a 500-character explanation for the parties (including the reasons for settlement or failure, the key points of any agreement, and the further options). (Editorial suggestion, not a hiring, qualification examination or skills test, and not a description of the procedure of any arbitration institution or mediation organisation.)

People who are more likely to adapt: those willing to do detailed work over the long term in document review, legal research and written output, able to keep records item by item where both precision and the consequences of error are demanding (65% consider precision or accuracy extremely important and 35% very important; 20% consider the consequences of error very serious and 30% serious), able to handle the demands of several parties at once and stay neutral and patient in conflict situations (45% face conflict situations every day and 20% at least once a week; 25% need to deal with unpleasant or angry people at least once a week), able to accept long hours of sitting from reading case files and writing hearing records (80% sit continually or almost continually, 47% work more than a 40-hour week and 63% have an irregular schedule), and able to disclose under procedures and withdraw in accordance with the law when under pressure from one party or where an interest relationship exists. The risk is usually greater for those who find it hard to accept that a conclusion may be challenged by the losing party or a party and may even enter setting-aside or review proceedings, who are unwilling to record the basis under procedures, or who lack a sense of boundaries about independence and confidentiality requirements.

Insufficient evidence: the national wage distribution for the exact occupation in China was not obtained this round. Current U.S. BLS basis: the May 2025 median annual wage is 75,530 US dollars; about 10,500 posts in 2025, growth of 5% over 2025—2035, a net increase of about 500 and an annual average of 300 openings. The older O*NET figures of 9,100 in 2024 and 3%—4% over 2024—2034 are used separately. Statutory appointment, the nature of the organisation and the pay for full-time and part-time work must be checked separately.

In one sentence: a neutral dispute handling post that takes disputes over contracts and other property rights and interests as its subject and, by reviewing materials, researching and applying the law, chairing hearings or mediation meetings, facilitating settlement or issuing an award and producing reviewable documents and records, delivers written opinions or awards, settlement agreements and procedural records; for mediation posts the outputs also include an agreement reached by the parties themselves.

The work of arbitrators, mediators and conciliators falls into four categories: dispute handling and procedural progress (holding an initial meeting with the disputing parties to explain the procedure and costs, chairing hearings or mediation meetings to obtain information and evidence, advancing procedural steps and deadlines, and determining the scope of liability under the evidence and the law and issuing an award or facilitating settlement); information gathering and evidence handling (reviewing claim applications, certificates and medical or employer records and similar materials, researching laws, regulations, policies and precedents, interviewing claimants, representatives or witnesses, and checking the chain and admissibility of the evidence); communication and negotiation (communicating with the disputing parties to clarify the issues and identify each party's real needs and interests, using mediation techniques to promote communication and understanding, guiding the parties to reach an agreement voluntarily, and negotiating on specialist disputes such as environmental ones); and documents and records (writing written opinions or awards, preparing settlement agreements, recording the procedure and outcome and maintaining case files).

O*NET 23-1022.00 Arbitrators, Mediators, and Conciliators: facilitating negotiation and conflict resolution through dialogue and handling disputes outside the court system with the joint consent of the parties. Common job titles listed on the page include alternative dispute resolution coordinator, arbiter, arbitrator, divorce mediator, family mediator, federal mediator, labour arbitrator, labour mediator, mediator and public employment mediator. The interest code is ECS (Enterprising, Conventional, Social); the page lists 20 tasks. The occupation requires extensive preparation (Job Zone Five, SVP 8.0 and above), and of the respondents 37% considered a professional degree necessary, 16% a bachelor's degree and 11% a post-baccalaureate certificate. The figures 37/16/11 are answers about the education needed by new entrants, not the education composition of current practitioners, and the Job Zone does not confer Chinese appointment qualifications.

entries: Case material review and fact organisation｜Fixing the materials and the issues first｜Reviewing claim applications, contracts, certificates, birth or death certificates and medical or employer records and similar materials, communicating with the disputing parties to clarify the issues and identifying each party's real needs and interests.

Legal research and application of the basis｜Supporting conclusions with a checkable basis｜Researching the relevant laws, regulations, policies and precedents, applying them to the facts of the case to reach a conclusion, and determining the scope of liability under the evidence and the law or administrative and judicial precedent.

Chairing hearings and mediation meetings｜Advancing under procedures while staying neutral｜Chairing hearings to obtain information or evidence and ruling on objections, motions and the admissibility of evidence, or chairing mediation meetings and using mediation techniques to promote communication and understanding.

Facilitating settlement and handling proposals｜Letting the parties reach an agreement voluntarily｜Guiding the parties to reach an agreement voluntarily, preparing settlement agreements, and advising on accepting or rejecting a settlement proposal and authorising payment of a valid claim. The U.S. task combination includes different arbitration and mediation roles, and people's mediation does not authorise the payment of claims; whether a settlement recommendation binds the parties is checked against the specific role and jurisdiction.

Awards and document writing｜Issuing reviewable documents to standard｜Writing written opinions or awards stating the facts found, the basis and the reasons, writing case records and procedural documents, and preparing court or testimony materials as required.

Procedural records and file management｜Maintaining records according to the actual procedure｜Recording the progress and outcome of the procedure, organizing and filing case materials, researching whether appeal and setting-aside procedures meet the legal requirements, and keeping files according to the actual procedure without promising full traceability.

Collaboration and competition｜15% consider working with a team very important, 15% important, 20% fairly important and 45% not at all important; 20% consider coordinating or leading others very important, 15% important, 15% fairly important and 45% not at all important; 50% consider competition highly fierce, 20% moderately competitive and 15% slightly competitive.
External communication and conflict handling｜21% consider dealing with external customers or the public very important, 16% important, 11% fairly important and 47% not at all important; 25% need to deal with unpleasant or angry people at least once a week but not every day (25% at least once a month but not every week and 35% at least once a year but not every month); 45% face conflict situations every day, 20% at least once a week but not every day, 15% at least once a month but not every week and 15% at least once a year but not every month.
Environment and posture｜25% work indoors in a controlled environment every day (15% at least once a week but not every day, 25% at least once a month but not every week and 25% never); 80% sit continually or almost continually and 15% sit more than half the time.
Written communication｜21% write letters and memos every day, 47% at least once a week but not every day and 21% at least once a month but not every week.
Work activities and skills focus｜The main work activities are getting information (91) and resolving conflicts and negotiating with others (91), followed by making decisions and solving problems (90), analysing data or information (85), evaluating information to determine compliance with standards (84), updating and using relevant knowledge (81), judging the qualities of objects, services and people (79) and interpreting the meaning of information for others (78). The U.S. work context bands are not shares of working time, an accident rate or Chinese job statistics; the activity ratings are not individual test scores.
Different dispute directions have different focuses; first check the applicable jurisdiction and authority, then review the evidence, hear the parties and produce documents.

The May 2025 annual median wage is 75,530 US dollars, with wage percentiles of 47,220 / 57,360 / 75,530 / 108,000 / 155,440 US dollars. Check the sources, procedure and reasons for the materials; keep confidentiality, disclose and withdraw in accordance with the applicable law, so that the documents are traceable and reviewable.

State the dispute and the applicable procedure → Explain the rules and the boundaries of voluntariness → Check the contract, records and sources of evidence → Compare the basis and the items still to be supplied → Hold the hearing or mediation and record the opinions → Produce the documents and keep the evidence index

The mainland China side follows the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China (adopted 1994-08-31, amended twice in 2009 and 2017, revised 2025-09-12, Presidential Order No. Fifty-Four, in force from 2026-03-01): arbitration institutions are established and registered in accordance with the law and are public-interest non-profit legal persons; arbitrators are appointed by the arbitration institution from persons who are fair and upright, have good professional quality and are diligent and responsible, and must meet one of the following conditions, namely having passed the national unified legal professional qualification examination and obtained the legal professional qualification and having worked in arbitration for at least eight years, having practised as a lawyer for at least eight years, having served as a judge or procurator for at least eight years, having engaged in legal research or teaching with a senior professional title, or having legal knowledge and having engaged in professional work in law, economics and trade, maritime affairs or science and technology with a senior professional title or an equivalent professional level; arbitration institutions set up arbitrator panels by specialism; arbitration is conducted independently in accordance with the law, free from interference by administrative organs, public organizations or individuals, and the award is final; Article 52 provides that proceedings are in principle not public, and may be public if the parties agree, except where state secrets, another person's trade secrets or personal privacy are involved. Also under the People's Mediation Law of the People's Republic of China (adopted 2010-08-28, Presidential Order No. Thirty-Four, in force from 2011-01-01): people's mediation committees are mass organizations established in accordance with the law to mediate civil disputes, and mediation charges no fee; people's mediators are served by members of the people's mediation committee and by persons appointed by it, and must be adult citizens who are fair and upright, enthusiastic about people's mediation work and have a certain level of education, policy understanding and legal knowledge; the judicial administration department of the State Council and the judicial administration departments of local people's governments at or above county level are responsible for guidance, and primary people's courts provide professional guidance; a mediation agreement reached through mediation is legally binding, and the parties may jointly apply to a people's court for judicial confirmation within thirty days from the date the agreement takes effect. This page does not constitute legal or examination advice. Ordinary conditions are distinguished from the appointment of persons from outside mainland China, the specific foreign-related formation of tribunals under Article 82 and specialist arbitration under Article 93, and not all mediation and arbitration is subject to the same conditions.
Insufficient evidence: the Chinese occupational classification mapping has not been verified.

Arbitrators make awards and mediators facilitate an agreement between the parties, while U.S. conciliators usually meet them separately; these three roles cannot be merged into a single adjudicative power. Chinese courts exercise judicial adjudicative power, and lawyers provide representation services for the parties in accordance with the law; administrative decisions are made by the competent organs. Labour dispute arbitration follows dedicated legislation, and the qualification and finality rules of civil and commercial arbitration cannot be applied to it.

Within the scope of the engagement or appointment, complete the material review and application of the basis and chair the hearing or mediation, and deliver reviewable awards or agreement documents and procedural records.

Answer dispute handling and document delivery questions with whether the matters in dispute and the applicable procedure are stated, whether the review of the materials and evidence and their sources are reviewable, whether the applicable law and basis are explained, whether the facts found and the reasons are disclosed, and whether the procedural records are complete.

Chinese civil and commercial arbitration does not hear disputes over marriage, adoption, guardianship, maintenance and inheritance or administrative disputes that should be handled by administrative organs in accordance with the law; labour disputes, rural land contractual management disputes and sports arbitration follow dedicated legislation. Community family mediation is not the same as family arbitration.

The subject is disputes over contracts and other property rights and interests between equal parties (together with civil disputes that may be mediated in accordance with the law) and the evidence and interests involved; the basis is the relevant laws, regulations, policies and precedents (such as the substantive rules on contracts, company law, labour and social security, intellectual property and maritime affairs, and the procedural rules on arbitration and mediation), the contracts, certificates and records submitted by the parties, and the principles of voluntariness and confidentiality.

This page corresponds to U.S. O*NET/BLS 23-1022.00. Arbitrators handle disputes and issue awards within the applicable authorization and procedure; mediators and conciliators help the parties communicate and reach a voluntary agreement and do not decide in their place. The shared tasks include reviewing materials, clarifying the issues, chairing meetings, writing documents and maintaining records. Civil and commercial arbitration in China follows the current Arbitration Law, and specialist arbitration such as labour arbitration follows separate law; people's mediation selects mediators and carries out work under the People's Mediation Law. U.S. BLS shows employment of about 10,500 in 2025, growth of 5% over 2025—2035 and 300 annual openings, and this O*NET update also shows 2025—2035; the exact EP figure of 4.7%, the rounded OOH figure of 5% and the ONET5—6% band are checked separately, and none is Chinese occupational statistics.

Case management systems, legal research and legislation databases, document and spreadsheet software, and online hearing or video conferencing tools can be used for material registration, precedent research, procedural step management and document drafting; some directions also use electronic case files and evidence organisation tools. Judgements about the admissibility of evidence, the finding of facts, the choice of the applicable law, mediation strategy and the conclusion remain the responsibility of the arbitrator or mediator and are recorded honestly, and tool output cannot replace procedural judgement and professional responsibility.

Confirm the procedure and authority → Disclose conflicts and explain the rules → Collect materials and check the issues → Research the current basis and hear the parties → Hold the arbitration hearing or voluntary mediation → Issue the award or record the agreement and file it.

Measured by whether the matters in dispute and the procedure are stated, whether the review of the materials and evidence is reviewable, whether the applicable basis and the reasons for the findings are explained, whether the principles of voluntariness and confidentiality are followed, and whether the documents and records are prepared and kept to standard, not by one party's satisfaction or a single outcome indicator.

Written opinions or awards, settlement agreements or mediation agreements, hearing and mediation records, evidence lists and source notes, conclusions of legal and basis research, statements of the facts found and the reasons, procedural step and deadline records, and case files and filing lists.

Responsibilities are divided according to the scope of the engagement and the law and institutional standards; before starting, check the institution's establishment, registration and business scope, the appointment or selection conditions and panel arrangements (whether the conditions for arbitrators under the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China or for people's mediators under the People's Mediation Law of the People's Republic of China are required), the procedural and confidentiality standards, the disclosure and withdrawal system for independence and conflicts of interest, the safety arrangements for court appearances or travel, and the retention and transfer requirements for case files.

Awards or agreements are made or facilitated by the arbitrator or mediator within the scope of the engagement; the hearing and adjudication of litigation cases are conducted by the people's court in accordance with the law; representation and legal opinions are provided by lawyers; administrative decisions are made by administrative organs in accordance with the law; notarial certification is made by notarial institutions; and the day-to-day management of labour relations is undertaken by the employer and the trade union.

Ordinary civil and commercial arbitrators in China satisfy the standards of conduct and one of the five conditions under Articles 21—23 of the current Arbitration Law, are appointed by the institution and are listed on panels by specialism; special foreign-related arbitration in the circumstances limited by Article 82 is checked separately. People's mediators are selected under Articles 13—14 of the People's Mediation Law, and labour disputes follow separate legislation. There is no uniform national licence in the United States, but some states or courts require certification, training or a professional licence; the O*NET education survey is not a statutory qualification.

Dispute handling must follow the legal and procedural standards: procedural records, evidence or the basis must not be forged, and no award inconsistent with the facts and the law may be made; independence and neutrality must be maintained, and where an interest relationship exists or there is improper influence from one party the person must withdraw, disclose or decline as required; arbitration is conducted in private in accordance with the law unless the parties agree otherwise, mediation must follow the principles of confidentiality and voluntariness, and the identity of the parties, trade secrets and personal privacy must be handled in accordance with confidentiality and personal information protection requirements.

When materials and statements conflict, the admissibility or authenticity of evidence is in doubt, a party does not agree to continue mediation, an undisclosed interest relationship exists or there is improper pressure from one party, the procedure should be suspended, the materials corrected or the limitations stated honestly, and withdrawal, disclosure or escalation should follow the law and institutional procedures, without improper handling because of case closure targets or performance pressure.

An outcome applies only to the specific matters in dispute, procedure, parties and evidential conditions; the same dispute may yield different conclusions under a different procedure or different evidence, a mediation agreement presupposes that the parties reach it voluntarily, a single mediation outcome must not be presented as a general rule, and documents that have not taken effect or been confirmed must not be treated as effective conclusions.

Check at least six things before starting: the work direction (labour and commercial arbitration, community and family mediation, administrative and public dispute mediation, environmental and natural resources dispute mediation and so on); the qualification and selection requirements (whether the conditions for arbitrators under the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China are met and the person is listed on a panel by specialism, or the conditions for people's mediators under the People's Mediation Law of the People's Republic of China are met, and the institution's business scope and appointment arrangements); the working pattern and intensity (long hours of sitting from reading case files and writing hearing records (80% sit continually or almost continually), the workweek and schedule (47% more than 40 hours, 63% irregular) and travel arrangements); the record and compliance requirements (standards for keeping records of procedure and evidence, the system for independence and withdrawal and disclosure, and confidentiality and personal information processing requirements); the employment and income form (full-time institutional posts, part-time appointment, payment per case or per item and whether court appearances and travel allowances are included); and the development path (deeper specialisation, being listed on a panel and handling complex cases, moving into review and management posts, or moving to lawyer, labour relations and compliance roles).
Look at the work direction and the nature of the institution, not the job title.

Work direction: labour and commercial arbitration, community and family mediation, administrative and public dispute mediation, environmental and natural resources dispute mediation, and in-house institutional dispute handling and compliance mediation; different directions differ in the type of dispute, the applicable basis, the procedural rules and the parties served.
The selection conditions and the institution's business scope determine whether cases can be handled and in what capacity one takes part in the procedure.

Qualifications and scope of handling: whether one of the conditions for arbitrators under the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China is met and the person is listed on the arbitrator panel by specialism, or the conditions for people's mediators under the People's Mediation Law of the People's Republic of China are met; the institution's establishment, registration, business scope and scope of acceptance; whether foreign-related arbitration or maritime affairs and similar cases with higher professional and language demands are involved; and whether a related professional background and practical experience are required.
The working pattern, intensity and record-keeping requirements directly affect whether the work can be completed compliantly and sustainably.

Working and compliance conditions: long hours of sitting and concentrated eye use from reading case files and writing documents, hearing or mediation meeting arrangements and travel, and the workweek and schedule regularity; the standards for keeping records of procedure and evidence, the system for independence and the withdrawal and disclosure of conflicts of interest, the confidentiality requirements for case materials and party information, and the file retention and transfer system.
The nature of the institution and fluctuations in case intake affect long-term sustainability.

Employment and income form: the stability and safeguards differ between full-time or appointed posts in arbitration institutions and mediation organisations, labour relations and compliance posts in enterprises, and law firms and consultancies; 47% work more than a 40-hour week and 63% have an irregular schedule, and the number of cases is related to economic activity and the volume of contractual and labour relations disputes, so it must be checked against the actual appointment and pay arrangements.
Deeper specialisation, being listed on a panel and handling complex cases determine long-term development and the occupational ceiling.

Development path: whether one can build stable professional expertise in a direction (labour and commercial arbitration, community and family mediation, administrative and public dispute mediation, environmental and natural resources disputes), be listed on the arbitrator panel under the conditions of the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China or appointed under the People's Mediation Law of the People's Republic of China and take on complex cases, move into review and institutional management posts, or move into law, labour relations and compliance, or corporate legal and dispute management.
First check the official and institutional requirements, then decide on the investment.

Rely on public information from the judicial administration departments, arbitration institutions, people's mediation organisations and institutions of learning to check whether the arbitrator appointment conditions, the people's mediator conditions and the selection procedure are compliant; do not readily trust guarantees of a pass or of affiliation from unofficial bodies, and do not take part in any arrangement involving forged materials or signing documents on someone else's behalf.

paragraphs: Suggested order of choice: first decide the direction (labour and commercial arbitration, community and family mediation, or administrative and public dispute mediation), then check the selection conditions and the institution's business scope (whether one of the conditions for arbitrators under the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China is met and the person is listed on a panel by specialism, or the conditions for people's mediators under the People's Mediation Law of the People's Republic of China are met; the institution's scope of acceptance and handling arrangements), and finally confirm the working pattern and intensity, the record-keeping and confidentiality requirements, the employment and income form and the development path. All directions share material review, application of the basis, chairing hearings or mediation and document writing skills; moving to an adjacent occupation requires filling gaps in different abilities and qualifications (court litigation procedure and adjudication rules, representation and legal opinions, labour relations and collective bargaining, compliance and regulatory rules, and legal document and research support), and the systems of responsibility differ, so a direct transfer is not possible.

The basis of comparison is checked public materials such as O*NET 23-1022.00, the BLS wages and employment shown on the O*NET page, the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook, the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China (revised 2025-09-12, in force from 2026-03-01) and the People's Mediation Law of the People's Republic of China (adopted 2010-08-28, in force from 2011-01-01); the adjacent occupation sections serve only to explain boundaries and do not mean that qualifications or duties can be transferred between them.

The table below compares the three directions within this occupation and three adjacent occupations, using the same comparison dimensions: occupational direction, core work and output, key differences, and who the choice suits better.

Handles disputes over contracts and other property rights and interests between equal parties and hears them under the arbitration agreement and procedure; the finality of the award remains subject to statutory setting-aside and refusal-of-enforcement review. Labour disputes do not follow this qualification and finality rule.
People who are willing to study commercial law and the rules of evidence over the long term and who can bear responsibility for an award.

Reviewing contracts and correspondence evidence, researching and applying the relevant law and precedent, chairing hearings to obtain evidence, ruling on objections and admissibility, making an award or organising mediation, and writing written opinions and procedural records.
Civil and commercial arbitration direction

The disputes are mostly civil disputes such as family, neighbourhood, consumer and labour disputes; the focus is on multi-party communication, emotional reassurance and facilitating a voluntary agreement, with no award made and voluntariness of the parties as the principle.
People who are willing to do multi-party communication and patient guidance and who can face conflict and emotion over the long term.

Accepting and chairing mediation, explaining the procedure and the principles of confidentiality and voluntariness, organising each party's claims, using mediation techniques to facilitate communication and agreement, drawing up the mediation agreement and following up its performance.
Community and family mediation direction

The coordination of public matters requires first checking the statutory authority and dedicated rules of the accepting body. Administrative disputes cannot be arbitrated under the civil and commercial arbitration law; a mediation post does not thereby acquire administrative decision-making power.
People who are willing to check procedural compliance and organise the policy basis and to write clear explanations.

Checking the procedural steps and the basis of authority, organising the policies and regulations, chairing coordination meetings or hearings, recording each party's views, writing explanations and handling recommendations and filing them.
Public affairs dispute coordination (specific authority checked separately)
Covers litigation and adjudication; cases are heard and decided on the basis of state judicial power, the conclusion has judicial force, and the procedural and evidential rules are stricter.
People who are willing to hear and decide cases under court procedure and take responsibility for the judgment.
Chairing the hearing and the court investigation, reviewing the evidence and applying the law, making a judgment or ruling and writing the adjudication document.
Judges, magistrates and justices of the peace (adjacent occupation)
Covers one party; the focus is on representation, legal opinions and negotiation, and the position serves the client, unlike neutral adjudication.
People who are willing to assert the rights of one party and to do representation and negotiation.
Accepting instructions to provide legal opinions, draft and review documents, take part in negotiation and act in arbitration or litigation and protect the client's lawful rights and interests.
Lawyer (adjacent occupation)

Covers the internal side of the employer; the focus is on collective bargaining, labour contracts, employee relations and dispute prevention, representing the organisation's position and making no neutral award.
People who are willing to handle employee relations, collective bargaining and dispute prevention inside an organisation.
Taking part in collective bargaining and labour contract management, handling employee grievances and labour relations disputes, running system and compliance training and keeping records.
Labour relations specialist (adjacent occupation)

After deciding on a direction, check the selection and handling requirements that actually exist in each direction (whether the conditions for arbitrators under the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China are met and the person is listed on a panel by specialism, or the conditions for people's mediators under the People's Mediation Law of the People's Republic of China are met; the institution's scope of acceptance and handling arrangements), the requirements of dedicated rules such as foreign-related and maritime affairs, and the confidentiality, personal information processing and file retention requirements.

items.title: How do the entry jobs and early tasks of arbitrators, mediators and conciliators compare?

values: Education, experience and statutory qualifications

United States: BLS usually requires a bachelor's degree and related experience; the O*NET37% professional degree, 16% bachelor's and 11% post-baccalaureate certificate are answers about the education needs of new hires, not the composition of current qualifications, and Job Zone Five is not a Chinese qualification standard. The typical BLS experience of less than 5 years and medium-term OJT are not Chinese uniform thresholds.

Mainland China side: arbitrators are appointed by an arbitration institution from fair and upright persons under the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China and must meet one of the statutory conditions (holding the legal professional qualification and having worked in arbitration for at least eight years, having practised as a lawyer for at least eight years, having served as a judge or procurator for at least eight years, holding a senior title in legal research or teaching, or having legal knowledge and having engaged in professional work in law, economics and trade, maritime affairs or science and technology with a senior title or an equivalent professional level), and are listed on a panel by specialism; people's mediators are served by members of the people's mediation committee and by persons it appoints and must be adult citizens who are fair and upright, enthusiastic about people's mediation work and have a certain level of education, policy understanding and legal knowledge.

Education and preparation ability must be checked against the specific post; the Chinese People's Mediation Law sets no uniform university education requirement, and the five conditions for civil and commercial arbitrators are not the same as a uniform degree threshold.
Appointment, confidentiality and withdrawal

Ordinary civil and commercial arbitration in China requires checking institutional appointment and the panel; the special foreign-related arbitration under Article 82 is checked separately against the specific conditions. Arbitration is in principle not public, and where the parties agree to publicity it remains private if state secrets, a third party's trade secrets or personal privacy are involved. People's mediation follows the principle of voluntariness and may be public or private, protecting privacy and trade secrets in accordance with the law.

Articles 45—48 of ordinary civil and commercial arbitration govern written disclosure, statutory withdrawal and the decision of the competent body; people's mediation is checked for its neutrality and confidentiality duties, and the arbitration withdrawal procedure is not applied uniformly. Material permissions are checked under the law and with the actual institution.

items.title: What do employers usually look at in recruitment?

values: Fictional materials and rules

Vendor A and buyer B signed a contract: 100 items at 1,000 yuan each; the price is written as 100,000 yuan in figures but as "one hundred and ten thousand yuan" in words, which conflicts. Delivery is agreed for June 1, and A says that all 100 items were delivered on June 3, while B says that only 90 are qualified and 10 await inspection. The parties have chosen a lawful civil and commercial arbitration procedure; this exercise reviews the materials only and no actual award is made.

Four items of evidence: E1 delivery note records 100 items on June 3 and bears only A's signature; E2 acceptance sheet records 90 qualified and 10 awaiting inspection, signed by B but undated; E3 the parties' email of June 4 agrees to supplementary testing of the 10 items, and A's June 5 email unilaterally claims that all are qualified; E4 test summary lists only 5 items as qualified, with no full report, sampling method or sample handover.

The party writes to ask about the time limit, the fee and the consequences of refusing mediation. Fictional exercise rules: a communication is arranged within 5 days of receiving complete materials, with no promise of a closing date; the simulated fee is 1% of the amount in dispute, no definite fee is quoted before the amount is verified, and this is not a real institution's fee standard. If both parties agree to the plan on June 10: first confirm the 90 undisputed items, then supplementary testing of the 10 items, with payment after A and B jointly confirm the amount. All names, dates and amounts are fictional.
Three deliverables

① Write a procedural memorandum: list the three issues of price, delivery and quality and mark the existing evidence and the items still to be supplied for each; do not find a breach of contract or damages at this stage. ② Prepare the four-row table E1—E4, listing the source, what can be proven, the gaps and the checking action; note whether each can alone support that all 100 items are qualified.

③ Write a neutral reply of no more than 500 characters explaining the simulated time limit and fee without passing yourself off as a real institution; also write the mediation opening and the plan record, distinguishing the proposed plan from the items the parties have confirmed.
Reference answers and checking criteria

Memorandum: the amounts 100,000 and 110,000 conflict, so the original contract, the payment and both parties' confirmation must be checked; the fact that June 3 is two days later than June 1 is only a date comparison and cannot establish liability, exemption or loss without supplementary evidence. List the 90 items and the 10 items separately and do not write all qualified as confirmed.

Evidence table: E1 supports only A's claim of delivery, so B's receipt or transport records must be supplied; E2 supports B's statement about quantity and quality, so the date and the record of how it was made must be supplied; E3 supports the June 4 agreement to supplementary testing, and A's unilateral June 5 email does not prove that all are qualified; E4 is only a test summary of 5 items, so the full report, method, samples and handover must be supplied. All four require hearing the other side, and the existing materials cannot alone prove that all 100 items are qualified.

Example reply: we will check the price, the delivery and the supplementary testing materials. Under the rules of this exercise, a communication is arranged within 5 days of complete materials, and the timing of service and supplementary evidence affects progress, so no closing date can be promised. The simulated rate is 1% of the amount in dispute; if it is verified as 100,000 yuan that is 1,000 yuan and if 110,000 yuan then 1,100 yuan, and no definite quotation is given for now. Mediation presupposes the voluntariness of both parties, and refusing mediation is not the same as refusing arbitration; where arbitration has begun it continues under the applicable procedure. Please supply the original contract, the date of receipt and the complete test report.

Opening and plan check: explain neutrality, voluntariness and confidentiality; each side states its case and then restates the issues. The June 10 plan is only a conditional arrangement, and the supplementary testing of 10 items and the confirmation of the amount and the payment date still await clarification by the parties; where confirmation is incomplete, do not write all settled. If mediation is refused or fails, record the status and continue under the original procedure, without compelling a signature.
Exercise and authority boundaries

All of this is an editorial simulation and does not replace legal training, arbitrator appointment or real institutional advice; no real case files, party information or internal templates are used. The reference answers are an approach to review, not a decision in the case.

paragraphs: The qualification for this occupation is mainly based on statutory selection conditions, with marked differences between jurisdictions: on the mainland China side, under the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China (adopted 1994-08-31, amended twice in 2009 and 2017, revised 2025-09-12, Presidential Order No. Fifty-Four, in force from 2026-03-01), arbitrators are appointed by an arbitration institution from persons who are fair and upright, have good professional quality and are diligent and responsible, and must meet one of the statutory conditions, namely having passed the national unified legal professional qualification examination and obtained the legal professional qualification and having worked in arbitration for at least eight years, having practised as a lawyer for at least eight years, having served as a judge or procurator for at least eight years, having engaged in legal research or teaching with a senior professional title, or having legal knowledge and having engaged in professional work in law, economics and trade, maritime affairs or science and technology with a senior professional title or an equivalent professional level; arbitration institutions set up arbitrator panels by specialism; arbitration is conducted independently in accordance with the law and the award is final; Article 52 provides that proceedings are in principle not public, and may be public if the parties agree, except where state secrets, another person's trade secrets or personal privacy are involved.

The People's Mediation Law of the People's Republic of China (adopted 2010-08-28, Presidential Order No. Thirty-Four, in force from 2011-01-01) provides that people's mediation committees are mass organizations established in accordance with the law to mediate civil disputes, and mediation charges no fee; people's mediators are served by members of the people's mediation committee and by persons appointed by it, and must be adult citizens who are fair and upright, enthusiastic about people's mediation work and have a certain level of education, policy understanding and legal knowledge; the judicial administration department of the State Council and the judicial administration departments of local people's governments at or above county level are responsible for guidance, and primary people's courts provide professional guidance; a mediation agreement reached through mediation is legally binding, and the parties may jointly apply to a people's court for judicial confirmation within thirty days from the date the agreement takes effect. This page did not verify a uniform Chinese occupational classification mapping for arbitration and mediation posts; it provides no unverified sub-category code and no institution's specific appointment conditions or pass rates. entries.question: What do arbitrators, mediators and conciliators do every day?

entries.answer: Arbitrators and mediators chair the procedure, review the materials and apply the basis and make an award or facilitate an agreement within the scope of the engagement or appointment; the hearing and adjudication of litigation cases are conducted by the people's court in accordance with the law; representation and legal opinions are provided by lawyers; administrative decisions are made by administrative organs in accordance with the law; labour and personnel disputes are handled by the labour and personnel dispute arbitration committee under dedicated rules; in-house employee relations and collective bargaining are handled by the labour relations specialist on behalf of the organisation; and compliance review and the implementation of regulatory requirements are the responsibility of the compliance officer. An arbitral award and a mediation agreement are lawful dispute resolution outcomes; they do not replace a court judgment, representation or an administrative decision.

entries.answer: The BLS May 2025 wage percentiles shown on the O*NET 23-1022.00 page are: an annual median of 75,530 US dollars (hourly 36.31 US dollars), a 10th percentile of 47,220 US dollars, a 25th percentile of 57,360 US dollars, a 75th percentile of 108,000 US dollars and a 90th percentile of 155,440 US dollars; the median annual wage is consistent with the 2025 data in the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook. entries.answer: On the U.S. side, the BLS projection shown on the O*NET 23-1022.00 page is average growth of 3% to 4% over 2024—2034 with an annual average of about 300 openings and about 9,100 employed in 2024; the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook separately gives growth of 5% over 2025—2035, a net increase of about 500 and an annual average of about 300 openings, and the two have different data periods, which this page labels separately. On the mainland China side, arbitrators and people's mediators are subject to statutory selection conditions and procedural management, and the number of cases is related to economic activity and the volume of contractual and labour relations disputes, but there is no published national employment projection. Moves are possible into judicial and court work, administrative adjudication, law and representation, paralegal and legal support, labour relations and collective bargaining, compliance and regulation, equal opportunity and anti-discrimination, and human resources management, but each direction has a different qualification and responsibility system; this page provides no individual employment prediction.

entries.answer: An arbitral award and a mediation agreement must be distinguished: mediation helps the parties negotiate voluntarily. Ordinary civil and commercial arbitrators in China are lawfully appointed and listed on a panel, and special foreign-related arbitration is checked separately under Article 82; people's mediators are selected in accordance with the law, so no one can perform statutory duties merely by calling themselves a mediator. A people's mediation agreement is legally binding, and judicial confirmation follows a separate procedure; tool drafts and individual outcomes must be verified and cannot be taken directly as general rules.
